bottleneck: Pig organs edited to remove porcine viruses and humanize surface antigens still face hyperacute and chronic rejection: residual xenoantigens, coagulation incompatibilities, and immune responses that no edit set has fully mapped. Early human recipients of pig hearts and kidneys survived weeks to months, not years. Each additional gene edit raises the risk of off-target effects in the donor animal, and the full set of edits needed for durable tolerance is unknown.
current_state: Multi-edited pigs (10+ knockouts/knockins) have enabled the first human xenotransplants under compassionate use. Durable, rejection-free survival is not yet demonstrated, and long-term immunosuppression remains required.

sources.title: Architecting the Future of Health: From Code to Cure

title: Xenotransplant rejection outlasts multi-gene edits
why_it_blocks: Organ shortage kills tens of thousands yearly while edited pig organs fail within months. Until edited organs survive long-term without crushing immunosuppression, xenotransplantation cannot relieve the donor crisis.
